head:
Executive Order
PLUMAS NATIONAL FOREST
CALIFORNIA
Under authority of the Act of Congress approved June 4, 1897 (30 Stat.,
11, 34-36), and on the reconmmendation of the Secretary of Agriculture, it
is hereby ordered that the boundaries of the Pluinas National Forest as
modified by the Proclamation of July 28, 1910, be further modified by elimi-
nating therefrom the following described land, in the State of California :
In T. 25 N., R. 9 E., Sec. 22: SEA NW4;
Mount Diablo Meridian.
And it appearing proper and necessary, in the interest of equal oppor-
tunity and good administration, that all of such excluded land subject to
disposition should be restored to entry in advance of settlement, it is hereby
ordered, pursuant to the authority reposed in me by the Act of September
30, 1913 (38 Stat., 113), that such land, subject to valid rights, shall be open to
enitry only for a period of twenty-eight days from and including 9 o'clock
a. In., standard time, on the fifty-sixth day from and after the date of this
order, and thereafter to disposition under any and all of the public land laws
applicable thereto.
WOODROW WILSON
THE WHITE HOUSE,
17 November, 1914t.
~No. 2086.1

head:
Executive Orber
It is hereby ordered that Dungeness Spit, an arm of land extending
from the north shore of the State of Washington into the Strait of Juan
de Fuca, as the same is shown upon the official plats of survey of townships
thirty-one north, ranges three and four west of the Willamnette Meridian,
on file in the General Land Office, and as segregated by the broken line
upon the diagram hereto attached and made a part of this order, be and
the same is hereby reserved and set apart for the use of the Department
of Agriculture as a refuge, preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
This order is not intended to abrogate the orders creating military and
lighthouse reservations located in part upon the same lands, nor shall it in
any manner interfere with the use of the lands for military or lighthouse
purposes, but rather, in addition to such uses, shall insure the protection
of the native birds therein.
It is unlawful for any person to hunt, trap, capture, wilfully disturb
or kill any bird of any kind whatever, or take the eggs of such bird within
the limits of this reserve, except under such rules and regulations as may
be prescribed by the Secretary of Agriculture.
Warning is expressly given to all persons not to commit any of the
acts herein enumerated, under the penalties prescribed by Section 84 of
the U. S. Penal Code, approved March 4, 1909 05 Stat., io88).
This reservation to be known as Dungeness Spit Reservation.
WOODROW WILSON
THE WHITE HOUSE,
20OJanuary, 1

head:
]Executive Orber
It is hereby ordered that Ediz Hook, an arm of land extending from
the north shore of the State of Washington into the Strait of Juan de
Fuca, as the same is shown upon the official plat of survey of Townships
31 North, Range 6 West of the Willamette Meridian, and as located
within the area and segregated by the broken line upon the diagram hereto
attached and made a part of this order, be and the same is hereby reserved
and set apart for the use of the Department of Agriculture as a refuge,
preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
This order is not intended to abrogate the order creating a lighthouse
reservation located in part upon the same lands, nor shall it in, any manner
interfere with the use of the lands for lighthouse purposes, but, rather, in
addition to such uses, shall insure the protection of the native birds therein.
It is unlawful for any person to hunt, trap, capture, wilfully disturb
or kill any bird of any kind whatever, or take the eggs of such bird within
the limits of this reservation, except under such rules and regulations as
may be prescribed by the Secretary of Agriculture.
Warning is expressly given to all persons not to commit any of the
acts herein enumerated, under the penalties prescribed by Section 84 of
the U. S. Penal Code, approved March 4, 1909 (3 Stat., 1o88).
